name: Fiachna

attributes.attribute: fathered a son on his daughter Mugain
snagged a talking worm while fishing

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Fiachna is an Irish hero name common in Irish mythology. The name may mean raven. Most bearers are minor heroes. A few stand out. Fiachna of Munster was an incestuous king. He had a son with his own daughter Mugain. This other bearer, Fiachna mac Báetáin, won a battle when his wife Caíntigern lay with the ocean deity Manannán Mac Lir. This Fiachna might have been a real king, but his parthenogenetic conception suggests a divine ancestor or a totem. Fiachna mac Dáire snagged a worm while fishing at Cuailnge in Ulster. The talking worm forecast a coming conflict over the region's bull. The worm carried the soul of a reborn swineherd; it later manifested as the Brown Bull Donn Cuailnge. Queen Medb of Connacht launched the Cattle Raid over that bull. A second worm, the swineherd's bitter enemy who became the White Bull Finnbennach, had advised Medb to wed Ailill mac Máta. The two bulls then met in an epic final battle.

okr.objective: Fiachna is an Irish hero name whose notable bearers shaped stories of kingship and the Cattle Raid.
key_results: The name Fiachna may mean raven.
Fiachna of Munster was an incestuous king who fathered a son on his daughter Mugain.
Fiachna mac Báetáin won a battle after his wife slept with the sea god Manannán Mac Lir.
Fiachna mac Dáire snagged a talking worm that foretold the Cattle Raid over Donn Cuailnge.
